answer: Before a new identity can claim a large payout, it must cross a canyon of trust: two established identities vouch for it in writing, staking their own standing. The payout desk checks both vouchers within a day; if the newcomer proves fake, the vouchers lose their established status and the claim is voided. An honest newcomer finds two peers easily, while 1,000 fakes would need 2,000 honest vouchers — a gap near 1,000 to 1. When one operator marched fifty fresh identities across the tundra on a single voucher, the desk found them all on the same narrow ledge and struck them down.
